This is the first banlog update since the ban reversals a month ago. During this period, not even spam bans were issued. Now that a period a reflection and discussion has transpired, Voat's rules are being enforced once again, and as we will see, Voat is not playing games with those who dance along the boundaries.

At the outset we see that Spam bans dominate the list, as per usual. Looking at the reports, and the unrecognizable usernames, and we see the kind of spam typical of any internet forum. To ban such spammers is merely a part of nature.

Beyond these, however, we see a number of bans for "Dox", and for anyone who has been in the unfortunate position of paying attention to the weeks of unending meta drama on Voat, this will come as no surprise. Now, amidst the plethora of Vote Manipulation bans that were reversed a month ago, there were also two bans for "Dox". These, too, were appealed at the time, as many users claimed that, like with Vote Manipulation, "Dox" was not defined well enough to enforce when grey areas are entered, such as the sharing of information already-shared by the "Doxxed" party. I myself even made a post arguing that undefined laws could not be justly enforced.

What I have since realized, however, is that Voat's rules are not undefined; they are simply imperfectly defined, and that's an important difference, since there is no man-made law or rule that is perfectly defined. It is for this reason that we have court systems, judges, appeals courts, and even Supreme Courts above these. It is for this reason that many nations depend on reference to a "reasonable person" and how he would act in any given situation (and this I like, for it in a sense subordinates the imperfect laws of man to the perfect natural law that contains reason and morality).

The point here is that Voat cannot survive if it is lawless, nor if it does not enforce its rules because they are imperfectly defined. Some amount of judgment will always be involved. Some notable users were banned these past few days, all for showing their willingness to hold Voat's rules in disdain, and even risk the welfare of real people by sharing very sensitive information about them and their families. Voat has no reason to condone this, no more than it has interest in tolerating Spam.

The fact of the matter is we are all rational creatures, we can all apprehend Logos, and so when Voat has plainly stated Rules that all can see, there is no excuse for violating them -- and certainly no reason to complain when such violations lead to account bans.

Stay vigilant, goats. Great things are ahead.
